items.headline: FERC rejects Oklo's bid to rejoin PJM's interconnection queue
items.what_happened: FERC issued an order on September 24, 2026 under Docket EL26-101 denying Oklo's complaint that had sought to force PJM to reinstate a 750 MW hybrid project — 150 MW of advanced nuclear generation plus 300 MW of fuel cells and 300 MW of gas-fired generation, near Richmond, Virginia — into PJM's current interconnection study cycle. PJM had withdrawn the project in August after citing application defects it said Oklo never fixed.
items.why_it_matters: The order confirms FERC will hold co-located nuclear-plus-generation projects to ordinary interconnection-queue discipline, adding at least 18 months of delay risk for any microreactor developer planning a hybrid or behind-the-meter deployment on PJM's grid.
items.binding_note: A final FERC order denying the complaint; Oklo can refile in PJM's next study cycle or use the Expedited Interconnection Track, open through December 31, 2027.

items.headline: TRISO-X finishes vertical construction on its Oak Ridge fuel plant
items.what_happened: TRISO-X, X-energy's fuel subsidiary, announced on September 24, 2026 that it completed vertical construction of the 214,000-square-foot TX-1 fuel fabrication facility in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, completing the building's primary structure and clearing the way for interior build-out and fuel-fabrication equipment installation.
items.why_it_matters: TX-1 is sized to produce about 700,000 TRISO-X pebbles a year, enough for up to 11 Xe-100-class reactors, so its construction pace is a trackable leading indicator of when a second qualified TRISO fuel source becomes available to microreactor buyers.
